gate_results.gate_id: D2-006-G5: Cost drag <= 50% of gross PnL

observations: RETROSPECTIVE: this report was authored after execution as part of WP-6c. Metrics are transcribed from DEC-0010, the H-010 trial_log entry, and the H-010 experiment notebook. H-010 produced positive full-period Sharpe of 0.46477526210643 and positive PnL, but Sharpe remained below the 1.0 promotion threshold, max drawdown reached 84.9723%, cost drag reached 75.8594% of gross PnL, and parameter sensitivity was fragile. The strategy failed 5 of 8 D2-006 gates, and DEC-0010 archived the candidate as a baseline NO-GO. Max-drawdown and cost-drag values are under pre-WP-5b pipeline semantics; per WP-5a/WP-5b audit conclusions the overall NO-GO verdict is unaffected by later pipeline fixes.
diagnostic_findings: 4h basis / premium mean reversion produced the strongest WP-4b1 4h cross-stream baseline but was still not promotable.
Positive PnL and Sharpe were insufficient because Sharpe remained below threshold and drawdown, cost drag, sensitivity, and concentration gates failed.
Cost drag reached 75.8594% of gross PnL, so the structural-dislocation signal was not strong enough to absorb modeled execution friction.
The +25% basis-z threshold variant flipped Sharpe negative, making the baseline too parameter-sensitive for Gate 4.
Future basis-family work should require materially different risk containment, stricter regime filtering, or separately justified lower-cost assumptions.
